items.title: Nick Brignola interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, July 28, 1997
items.q: But anyway, I’d met him that night and right until he died we were very good friends.

ctx.x: I pulled out my now-famous duct taped Leonard Feather book from about ‘68, and I wanted to read something, and wonder if you actually said this. It said your “ambition is to become one of the top five baritone sax players in jazz.” And, well since you did that about twenty-five years ago, what’s your more recent goal been?

Oh, I don’t know. My recent goal is to survive. I originally said that because I was in the process of figuring out whether I was going to be a baritone sax player or just be an alto player, which was my first saxophone. But through the efforts of Harry Carney, who always kept encouraging me to be a baritone player, I figured, well, between Harry Carney and all these other guys like Gerry Mulligan and all of that – that’s like three or four -- so if I could just be one of the five guys. So it was that kind of…
I was wondering how that, when he did that, did he have different people going out and —
